statement: Anas: he ordered the mosque built; the plot had graves of idolaters, uneven ground and date palms; graves were dug up, ground levelled, palms cut and set toward the qiblah; they chanted 'O Allah, there is no good but the good of the Hereafter, so help the Ansar and the Emigrants'.
notes: Machine-checked for the first part; the chant is in the remainder of the narration (also Bukhari 3932), from memory.

statement: He carried bricks himself during the building.
The mosque had walls of unbaked brick, pillars of palm trunk and a roof of palm branches; rooms for his family adjoined it.
notes: Bukhari 446 (Ibn Umar) on the materials, number from memory, not machine-checked.

statement: Ibn Umar: the Muslims used to gather and estimate the time of prayer; a bell and a horn were suggested.
notes: Machine-checked. This narration credits Umar with suggesting that a man call out.

statement: Abdullah ibn Zayd saw in a dream a man who taught him the words of the adhan; the Prophet said it was a true vision and told him to teach Bilal, whose voice carried further.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the opening; graded hasan sahih (al-Albani, al-Arna'ut). The Prophet's words are in the remainder of the narration, from memory.

statement: Bilal was the first to call the adhan; he is the one who was dragged through Makkah saying 'Ahad, Ahad'.
The Emigrants came with nothing; the Ansar had land; the Ansar gave them a share of the date harvest in return for work.
He paired Emigrants and Ansar as brothers; Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi offered Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf half his wealth; he replied with a blessing and asked for the market, and earned curd and butter that day.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against all three. Sa'd's offer regarding his wives is not narrated.

statement: The people of as-Suffah lived in the mosque without family or property; Abu Hurayrah called them the guests of Islam.
notes: Machine-checked for the opening; 'the people of as-Suffah were the guests of Islam' is later in the same narration, from memory.

statement: Al-Bara: he prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months and loved to face the Ka'bah; after the change a man who had prayed with him told Ansar praying toward Jerusalem and they turned during their prayer.
